one_liner: SEO platform exposing backlink, keyword, and ranking data via API
blocker: Full API access requires an eligible paid Ahrefs plan; non-eligible plans get only limited free test queries

evidence.claim: API key authentication; keys created/managed by workspace owners and admins
evidence.quote: To send requests to Ahrefs API, you'll need an API key. Only workspace owners and admins can create and manage API keys.

evidence.claim: OAuth 2.0 supported for third-party integrations via Ahrefs Connect
evidence.quote: All API calls require authorization and are made on behalf of an authorized Ahrefs user. To do this, your app must obtain an API access token for that user.

evidence.claim: Full API access is gated to eligible paid plans; other plans get only free test queries
evidence.quote: Ahrefs API is available on [eligible paid plans](https://ahrefs.com/pricing). On all other plans, you'll still have access to a [limited set of free test queries]

evidence.claim: Broad REST API v3 surface across many product areas, with OpenAPI spec
evidence.quote: Currently, API v3 allows you to pull data from the Site Explorer, Keywords Explorer, SERP Overview, Rank Tracker, Site Audit, Brand Radar and Social Media Management endpoints

evidence.claim: Vendor ships an official hosted MCP server
evidence.quote: Ahrefs provides a hosted MCP server that allows users with a Lite plan or higher to connect their Ahrefs account to supported AI tools.

notes: Official hosted MCP server documented on vendor docs (Lite plan+). Usage-based pricing: most endpoints consume API units (min 50 units/request); consumed units are non-refundable. Ahrefs Connect OAuth apps start Inactive and need approval/activation for production. Third-party blogs conflict on which plans include API access (one claims Enterprise at $1,499/mo, another says bundled from Lite $129/mo); official docs only state 'eligible paid plans'. Free test queries allow development without consuming units.
